_comment: P28 · tables whose index size is larger than their heap, each with the written reason (≥ 40 chars). Judged only when the heap is ≥ 1 MB (docs/evidence/d1/P28/index-ratio-rule.md §2). Must equal the list inside supabase/migrations/PROBE_p28_index_ratio.sql — the build check compares them.
public.email_send_log: Production 2026-10-30 12:43 UTC (run 41057438794): heap 3136 kB, indexes 3656 kB (5). Each index is required or used: idx_email_send_log_message (message_id) 1080 kB, 11,673 scans — the queue's per-message lookups; idx_email_send_log_message_sent_unique (message_id, partial) 744 kB, 7,930 scans — the at-most-once send guard; email_send_log_pkey 912 kB; idx_email_send_log_created 696 kB (9 scans) and idx_email_send_log_recipient 224 kB (3 scans) serve admin listing and suppression lookups. Text message ids make the indexes wide relative to a narrow log row. The real lever is a retention window for this log (P26 scope decision), not an index drop; low-use candidates wait for the C-2 hold.
public.posts: Staging 2026-10-04 08:17 UTC: heap 2.9 MB, indexes 6.8 MB (12). 3.25 MB of that is idx_posts_content_trgm (GIN trigram on content), the only content-search path until P20 names a search engine; it goes when P20 replaces it. Redundant candidates (idx_posts_user_id, a prefix of idx_posts_user_id_created_at; idx_posts_content_hash, 0 scans) are listed for A-4c and stay until the C-2 hold on index drops is reconciled.
